title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Team Members
tiers.description: All directors, officers and employees of the Group and any contractor or consultant whose terms of engagement with the Group apply this Policy to them.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, members of the Executive Leadership Team and the Company Secretary, and any other person advised in writing that they are a Designated Person. Subject to Trading Window approval, margin lending prohibition and Connected Party obligations.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: Sub-group of Designated Persons distinguished only for clearance: approved by the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Directors (other than the Chair of the Board)
tiers.description: Sub-group of Designated Persons distinguished only for clearance: approved by the Chair of the Board.

tiers.name: Designated Persons (other than the Directors and the Company Secretary)
tiers.description: ELT members and other notified Designated Persons, distinguished only for clearance: approved by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Company Secretary
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: approved by the Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer.

tiers.name: Connected Parties
tiers.description: A Designated Person's family members who may influence or be influenced by them, and companies or entities the Designated Person can control (including family trusts or superannuation funds where they are trustee or beneficiary).

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or the Company Secretary (or their delegates) has discretion not to open a Trading Window, or to impose an additional blackout period during a Trading Window. If a dealing request is refused or an approval revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. 'Deal' is described (in the insider trading section) as including exercising options over securities, so an OTC put/call would be a dealing, but ordinary Team Members are not subject to a clearance or Trading Window regime -- only the insider trading, front page test and short-term/speculative dealing rules apply.
rules.evidence: buy or sell securities in a company, or enter in an agreement to buy or sell securities, or exercise options over securities, or otherwise apply for, acquire or dispose of securities (deal)

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule, but 'deal' extends to exercising options over securities, and Designated Persons may only deal (in or outside a Trading Window) with prior written approval from the relevant Approval Officer.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may only deal in the Company's securities during the following Trading Windows if they apply for and receive prior approval for the proposed dealing

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging equity-plan securities before they vest, applying to all Team Members including Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: Company securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging plan securities that are vested but still subject to a plan holding lock or dealing restriction.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Once vested and free of any holding lock, hedging is not itself named as prohibited; it is only caught as an ordinary dealing, subject to the insider trading and short-term/speculative dealing rules, with no clearance requirement for non-Designated Team Members.
rules.evidence: Hedging includes entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Once vested and unrestricted, hedging is treated as an ordinary dealing requiring prior written approval and confinement to a Trading Window.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may only deal in the Company's securities during the following Trading Windows if they apply for and receive prior approval for the proposed dealing

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. a prepaid forward) is not named. It would fall within 'enter in an agreement to buy or sell securities', a dealing, but non-Designated Team Members face no clearance regime, only the general dealing restrictions.
rules.evidence: enter in an agreement to buy or sell securities, or exercise options over securities, or otherwise apply for, acquire or dispose of securities (deal)

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named; caught as a dealing requiring prior written approval and confinement to a Trading Window.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may only deal in the Company's securities during the following Trading Windows if they apply for and receive prior approval for the proposed dealing

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling for all Team Members, framed as part of the ban on speculative dealing.
rules.evidence: Team Members must also not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short‐selling.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and is not covered by the description of 'deal' used for the insider trading rules.

CFDs are not named, but the ban on dealing 'on a speculative basis' would in substance catch a CFD referencing the Company's securities, especially given the Policy's stated substance-over-form approach.
rules.evidence: Team Members must also not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short‐selling.

rules.detail: Designated Persons may not enter a margin lending arrangement over Company securities or transfer Company securities into an existing margin loan account. Not expressed to extend to other Team Members.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not enter into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities or transfer securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.

rules.detail: The margin lending prohibition in 4.6 is expressed to apply only to Designated Persons; it is silent for other Team Members.
Granting a charge, lien or pledge over Company securities generally (outside a margin lending arrangement) is not named and is not captured by the description of 'deal'.

Only 'margin lending arrangements' and transfers into 'an existing margin loan account' are prohibited (4.6); a broader secured financing arrangement not structured as a margin loan is not expressly addressed.

Objective ban on buying and selling on market within 3 months, and on entering 'other short term dealings' such as forward contracts, for all Team Members. Carve-out for selling vested plan shares within 3 months of vesting.
rules.evidence: Short‐term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

exemption_authority: The relevant Approval Officer (Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, Chair of the Board, Company Secretary or the CEO, per the table in 4.4) may approve dealing during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order (4.3); the Approval Officer need not give reasons, may impose conditions, and may revoke approval at any time (4.4(c)), and any refusal or revocation is kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights [is an Excluded Dealing not subject to sections 3.3, 4.1 and 4.2]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is excluded from both the short-term dealing ban and the Trading Window/blackout restriction, so it is not blocked by a closed window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not enter into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities or transfer securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is confined to margin lending and margin loan accounts; a bespoke pledge-secured loan not structured or documented as a margin loan is not expressly captured, though the Policy's substance-over-form approach could still be invoked against it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short‐term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar (paired forward-like derivative positions) risks being characterised as a prohibited 'other short term dealing' irrespective of the 3-month on-market test, so structuring and tenor should be cleared with the Company Secretary in advance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Approval Officer is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision, and may revoke their approval at any time. If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar could be revoked without reasons before execution, so the bank cannot treat clearance as final until both legs are signed within the validity window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the approved dealing must occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective and fresh approval must be sought.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of both collar legs must complete within 5 business days of approval or a fresh clearance application is required.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A publicised leveraged hedge around an executive's shareholding could be refused on reputational grounds even where otherwise compliant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Parties only deal in securities in circumstances where the Designated Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the Trading Window, margin-lending or hedging restrictions.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted shares appears workable for Designated Persons (directors, ELT, the Company Secretary and other notified persons) subject to prior written approval from the applicable Approval Officer, confined to an open Trading Window, and executed within 5 business days of approval. Hedging is only expressly banned while shares are unvested or subject to a plan holding lock; once vested and unrestricted, entering into the put/call is an ordinary dealing requiring clearance rather than being prohibited outright. The Policy's only financing restriction bans 'margin lending arrangements' and transfers into an 'existing margin loan account', which is narrower than a full secured-financing ban, so a bespoke pledge-secured loan not structured as a margin loan is not expressly caught, though this should be confirmed given the Policy's substance-over-form approach. Usefully, a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights is an Excluded Dealing, exempt from both the short-term dealing ban and the Trading Window restriction, so the bank's enforcement sale is not blocked by a closed window. Residual risks are the ban on 'other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts)', which could catch a short-tenor collar, and the Approval Officer's unfettered, confidential discretion to refuse or revoke clearance under the Front Page Test.
